threads.body:
@copilot Update this pull request directly with one focused fixture-lifecycle correction. Keep its Spring JMS 2.0 baseline, compatibility range, receive-suppression implementation, isolated version20Test and version30Test suites, and telemetry behavior unchanged. Do not create another PR.

In instrumentation/spring/spring-jms/spring-jms-2.0/javaagent/src/version20Test/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/spring/jms/v2_0/SpringJmsBaselineTest.java, the fixture registers cleanup.deferCleanup(container::stop). Both the Spring 2.0 and 3.0 suites use this test. stop pauses message delivery but is not full disposal. In Spring 3.0, AbstractJmsListeningContainer.doStop only clears running and stops the shared connection; active remains true. destroy calls shutdown, which also clears active, wakes and terminates invokers, waits for shutdown, and releases the shared connection. The current cleanup can leave invokers and JMS resources alive while the connection factory and broker are subsequently closed.

Register full listener-container destruction, such as container::destroy, before initialization so cleanup safely handles successful and partially completed setup. Verify this lifecycle choice against both Spring 2.0 and 3.0. Keep disposal ordered before connection-factory closure and broker shutdown, and retain the existing deferred-cleanup protection. Avoid unrelated changes.

Run the relevant version20Test, version20TestReceiveTelemetryEnabled, and version30Test executions, plus any narrowly necessary regression checks. Record exact commands and outcomes in the coding-session evidence, including blockers. Preserve the intended default-off receive telemetry, explicit receive-enabled coverage, process context and durable-subscription assertions. The earlier coding task is completed, and Copilot review 5617529273 on a35bec9c80373d02fb4a27f8d521796cff3528f7 reported no findings; this follow-up addresses the coordinator's independently verified cleanup defect.

replies.body: Updated in 9553fec8: deferred cleanup now calls `container.destroy()` before factory closure and broker shutdown. The requested `version20Test`, `version20TestReceiveTelemetryEnabled`, and `version30Test` tasks all passed (1 test each, no failures). The only environment warning was unavailable DNS for the remote Gradle build cache; it did not block the run.

@copilot Simplify the implementation in this PR directly without weakening its coverage or changing its behavior. The user requested this simplification pass. Keep this PR's existing head branch, base and draft state; do not create another PR. Scope is instrumentation/spring/spring-jms/spring-jms-2.0/javaagent and directly relevant existing build helpers.

In src/version20Test/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/spring/jms/v2_0/SpringJmsBaselineTest.java, remove the span-search round trip. Assert the listener's captured context against the process span inside the complete trace assertion. Eliminate findProcessSpan(), the producer-span return value, and scans of testing.spans(). Share the identical parent-trace assertion between receive-enabled and disabled modes, using an ordinary local trace assertion if appropriate rather than introducing a new abstraction. Retain whatever producer reference is genuinely necessary for asserting the separate receive trace's link.

Replace the message-received CountDownLatch plus AtomicReference<SpanContext> with a CompletableFuture<SpanContext> completed by the listener, then await its value with the existing bounded timeout. Keep the separate consumer-readiness synchronization that prevents publishing to a topic before subscription registration. Preserve a concrete instrumentable SessionAwareMessageListener compatible with the nongeneric Spring 2.0 interface; do not accidentally replace it with an uninstrumented lambda.

In build.gradle.kts, use the repository's existing JvmTestSuite executions helper for version20Test's ReceiveTelemetryEnabled execution instead of manually repeating testClassesDirs, classpath and check wiring. The helper lives in conventions/src/main/kotlin/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/gradle/TestSuiteExecutions.kt, supplies those bindings and check dependencies, and is already used by instrumentation/spring/spring-ai-1.0/javaagent/build.gradle.kts. Use the existing helper, do not modify or add shared build infrastructure for this narrow change.

In JmsReceiveInstrumentation, simplify the three type-name alternatives using namedOneOf, and the two receive-method alternatives using namedOneOf with their shared MessageConsumer argument matcher applied once. Preserve matching of the actual supported legacy receiveMessage and modern receiveFromConsumer implementations, including scoped suppression and cleanup; check concrete signatures before removing redundant predicates.

Try removing the blanket org.springframework version-forcing and Spring Boot exclusion block for version20Test/version30Test. These suites already declare isolated dependencies and do not inherit modern test output or testImplementation. Inspect the resolved compile and runtime graphs without those rules. Remove the block if the exact intended Spring 2.0 and 3.0 runtimes remain intact. If a real transitive upgrade remains, address the identified dependency narrowly or retain only the rule demonstrated necessary, and record the dependency evidence in your session output. Do not drop the explicit Spring 3.0 spring-tx dependency merely because spring-jms publishes it as optional. Do not add module-specific runtime version assertions or a repository-wide drift detector.

Keep BOTH version20Test and version30Test because they cover different receive-method owners. Keep the existing default-off and explicit receive-enabled executions, full container::destroy cleanup registered before initialization and ordered before factory/broker closure, legacy durable-subscription naming, context propagation, exact complete trace assertions, and consumed-message metric ownership. Preserve the supported minimum 2.0, compatibility range [2.0,6), module selectors, scope identity, sibling Muzzle selection, and existing modern receive-enabled/disabled and JMS-disabled coverage. Avoid unrelated fixture rewrites, new abstractions, and reducing assertions simply to shorten the file.

Run the narrow formatter and relevant version20Test, version20TestReceiveTelemetryEnabled, version30Test and affected existing behavior tests. Verify both isolated compile/runtime dependency graphs after simplifying resolution, and perform the relevant Muzzle checks when feasible. Record exact commands and outcomes in coding-session evidence, and disclose environmental blockers. Do not wait for CI. The coordinator will inspect delivery and request a fresh Copilot review of the resulting head.
